name: Ashes

global_influences.artist_or_genre: Western folk rock / alternative rock traditions (general)
global_influences.evidence: Ashes is characterized as a rock band with a folk rock subgenre, distinguished by strong vocals, catchy melodies and emotionally resonant lyrics — a stylistic profile consistent with the broader folk-rock/alternative influence vectors documented for the genre in the BMEM framework, though specific artist-level influence citations were not found in available sources.

local_adaptation_notes: Formed in 2006 by three friends (Evan, Rafsan, Bijoy) who only began seriously composing original material by 2009, Ashes represents the mid-2000s wave of alternative/folk-rock bands emphasizing melodic songwriting and emotionally direct Bangla lyrics over technical complexity, distinguishing the band from the progressive-metal-oriented alternative scene.
sound_evolution_summary: Formative period (2006–2009): founded by Evan, Rafsan and Bijoy; expanded lineup with Towhid and Tanim; spent the first three years developing musical direction before committing seriously to original composition in 2009. Debut period (2010): first mixed album released 5 November 2010, establishing the band's folk-rock-inflected alternative sound with the now-current lineup (Evan, Rafsan, Turjo, Adnan).
concert_culture_notes: Specific concert/festival data not yet documented in available sources — flagged for further research; band is described as one of the more popular acts in the country, suggesting an active live circuit presence.
listener_community_notes: Grouped within the Alternative/Indie genre alongside Meghdol, Shohojia and Conclusion in the BMEM framework, appealing to listeners drawn to melodic, emotionally resonant Bangla songwriting over harder rock/metal aesthetics.
